item.text: {"analysis":"The trial timed out after 337.02 allocated GPU-seconds and returned no validation score. Model quality and completion of all four categories therefore remain unknown. The configured 450-second per-category guard exceeds the observed allocation for the entire trial, so it cannot ensure completion. Candidate-specific attention across sampled transitions and gradient-checkpoint recomputation are plausible runtime costs, but no diagnostics establish the bottleneck. Future attempts should fit all four categories within the total allocation, reduce scoring cost, and measure runtime before drawing quality conclusions.","code_summary":"One independent SASRec model per category: 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, maximum history length 64, and dropout 0.2. A jointly trained candidate-attention branch pools causal history features and adds a gated residual to the sequential representation. Scores use normalized item embeddings, learned temperature, and item bias. Training uses AdamW, sampled-softmax cross-entropy, up to four transitions per history, and 64 shared sampled negatives with training-history exclusions. Local validation selects one checkpoint per category; the predictor writer loads the matching architecture and routes each dataset to exactly one checkpoint. No ensembles or checkpoint averaging are used."}
